record.summary: Lakshmi Reddy (68) died 14 months ago, leaving a house and a small agricultural plot. Two weeks before her death, while hospitalized for kidney failure and on sedatives, a typed will dated 9 days before her death was signed, favoring her son Suresh, who was also a witness along with a hospital clerk. The will was not registered. After the funeral, her other children Anita (abroad) and Kiran (another city) learned of the will, which contradicts a handwritten note from 6 years ago stating the three children should share equally. Suresh claims he cared for Lakshmi and that she freely chose to reward him. He has begun mutating the property in his name and listed the land for sale. Anita and Kiran wish to contest the will and stop the sale.
record.goal: To contest the will, halt the sale of the land, and assess the likelihood of success.
questions: What is the exact date of Lakshmi Reddy's death?
Do you have a copy of the will showing the date and signatures?
Where is the house and the agricultural land located (state/district)?
Did any doctor provide a medical certificate of Lakshmi's mental capacity on the day the will was signed?
Can you provide the names and contact details of the two witnesses mentioned in the will?
contradictions: The story says the will was signed "two weeks before her death," while the will itself is dated "9 days before Lakshmi's death."
evidence: The will is a typed one-page document dated 9 days before Lakshmi's death, signed with a shaky signature and witnessed by two people: the hospital's administrative clerk and Suresh's friend. It was not registered.

Hospital records show Lakshmi was admitted for kidney failure and was receiving sedatives and pain medication, and a nursing note from the day before the will records her as "intermittently confused, oriented to person only." There is no doctor's certificate of capacity on the day of signing.
An earlier handwritten note from 6 years ago, found by Anita in a family album, says "all three children should share equally," but it is unwitnessed and unsigned beyond initials.
Suresh's bank statements show he paid most of the hospital bills, which supports his caregiving claim.
A cousin states that Suresh asked Lakshmi to "sign something" in hospital and she "didn't seem to know what it was," but the cousin was not present for the signing.
The property listing for the land is already live online, and the municipal record shows Suresh's mutation application filed three weeks ago, still pending.
